project_type: Next.js 15 + TypeScript + Tailwind CSS + Framer Motion + GSAP
test_framework: No test framework configured (no tests directory, no test runner in package.json)
verification_instructions: 1. Run `npm run build` to verify the build passes without errors. 2. Check that next.config.ts is valid TypeScript. 3. Verify the service worker file exists in public/. 4. Confirm useSequencesPreload.ts loads only 50 critical thumbnails initially.
setup_instructions: node_modules already installed, no additional setup needed
environment_constraints: Vercel deployment. No Docker. Build validation via `npm run build`.
key_patterns: - All frame sequences in public/{folder}/frame-{001-150}.webp and public/{folder}-thumb/frame-{001-150}.webp. - useSequencesPreload hook manages progressive loading (thumbnails first then full-res). - HomeExperience.tsx defines sequences with FRAME_COUNT=150 and priority settings. - ImageSequencePlayer.tsx reads frames from imagesRef imperatively. - No service worker exists yet. No vercel.json exists yet.
directory_structure: Root: next.config.ts, package.json, vercel deployment. src/app/ - Next.js app router pages. src/components/ - UI components including Hero, Preloader, story/ImageSequencePlayer. src/hooks/ - useSequencesPreload.ts (critical preloading), useScrollProximityLoader.ts (lazy trigger). public/ - Static assets: 1st-vdo/ through 4th-vdo/ (150 frames each, 960x540 webp), 1st-vdo-thumb/ through 4th-vdo-thumb/ (150 frames each, 240x135 webp thumbnails).
